# Proposal: Soften build/plan ADV_SYNC cross-reference

## Problem

During `fixSubAgentMcpRouting` AC4, the user base files `~/.config/opencode/agents/build.md:161` and `plan.md:158,162` were rewritten with mode-neutral routing prose that includes the clause "See the ADV_SYNC block at the top of this prompt for routing guidance (catalog-via-execute when exposed, direct callables otherwise)".

For `explore` and `general`, this cross-reference is accurate — their ADV_SYNC overlays contain the canonical `MCP_ACTIVE_SURFACE_CONTRACT`.

For `build` and `plan`, this cross-reference is **misleading** — their ADV_SYNC overlay blocks (per design AD8/OOS5 of fixSubAgentMcpRouting) do NOT contain the canonical contract line. The contract for build/plan lives in advance-source body files (`.opencode/agents/build.md:171-179`, `.opencode/agents/plan.md:170-179`) which are NOT applied to user-owned deployed files by `deploy-local.sh` (only overlays are injected).

Functional behavior is preserved — build/plan agents still receive the routing contract via the always-on global `~/.config/opencode/instructions/lgrep-tools.md` instruction loaded into every OpenCode agent. But the in-file cross-reference is technically wrong for these two files.

## Proposed direction

Minimum-viable doc fix: soften the cross-reference wording in user `build.md` and `plan.md` so it no longer claims the ADV_SYNC block contains routing guidance it doesn't.

Replacement wording: drop the "See the ADV_SYNC block..." clause and rely on (a) the existing mode-neutral preference prose ("Reach for the highest-fidelity capability exposed on your surface before falling back to `grep`/`read`") plus (b) the always-on global `lgrep-tools.md` instruction that already teaches the mode-aware routing contract.

## Why not the architectural option

The deeper OOS5 option (centralize build/plan contract from source body to overlay, coordinated with C7 exactly-once invariant) is a separate larger change. This proposal addresses only the doc-gap introduced by AC4 — the misleading cross-reference. The architectural centralization remains a future option.

## Scope

- In scope: 3 line edits across 2 user config files (`~/.config/opencode/agents/build.md`, `plan.md`)
- Out of scope: advance-repo source files; overlay files; effective-prompts modeling; architectural centralization; lgrep-tools.md global instruction
- No spec deltas; no tests (prose-only change to user config files outside any git repo); no deploy step (edits are direct filesystem writes to active config)

## Verification

- Re-read each edited file to confirm the cross-reference is removed/softened
- Confirm frontmatter and ADV_SYNC block content unchanged
- Confirm routing preference prose still present (mode-neutral)

# Design: Soften build/plan ADV_SYNC cross-reference

## Architecture decisions

### AD1 — Minimum-viable doc fix vs architectural centralization

**Chosen:** minimum-viable doc fix (remove/soften the misleading cross-reference).

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Option a — Architectural centralization:* move build/plan contract from advance-source body (`.opencode/agents/build.md:171-179`, `plan.md:170-179`) into their overlays, coordinated with C7 exactly-once invariant. Would require: (i) editing 4 advance-source files, (ii) updating `tool-name-assets.test.ts` overlay-only filter expected list to include build/plan, (iii) deploy + verify. **Rejected for this change:** larger scope, multi-file advance-repo edits, requires contract-centralization decision. Tracked as OOS1 for separate change.
- *Option b — Soften cross-reference wording:* replace "See the ADV_SYNC block..." with neutral wording like "Discover the active surface per the global routing contract" or just drop the clause. **Chosen:** minimum-viable, user-file-only, preserves fixSubAgentMcpRouting ship state.

### AD2 — Replacement wording

For each of the 3 cross-reference sites, drop the "See the ADV_SYNC block at the top of this prompt for routing guidance (catalog-via-execute when exposed, direct callables otherwise)" clause. The remaining mode-neutral preference prose already teaches the right behavior:
- `build.md:161`: "Reach for the highest-fidelity capability exposed on your surface before falling back to `grep`/`read`." (retained)
- `plan.md:158`: "If `lgrep` (or its equivalent under your active tool surface) fails or times out once, fall back immediately to `glob`/`grep`/`read` for that turn." (retained)
- `plan.md:162`: "Use Exa for general search and Firecrawl/webfetch for web content extraction. For library/framework/API documentation, **use Context7 directly** — don't default to delegating to `libian`." (retained; mode-aware routing supplied by global `lgrep-tools.md` instruction)

The drop is safe because:
- Functional routing is preserved by global `~/.config/opencode/instructions/lgrep-tools.md` always-on instruction (verified during fixSubAgentMcpRouting harden).
- The retained prose still teaches preference for highest-fidelity capabilities (mode-neutral).
- No env-var conditionals or per-agent branching introduced.

## Implementation strategy

Direct filesystem edits to 2 user config files. No worktree needed (not in any git repo). No tests (prose-only; no behavior change).

## Verification strategy

Re-read each edited file post-edit:
- Confirm cross-reference clause removed at the 3 sites
- Confirm frontmatter unchanged (lines before body)
- Confirm ADV_SYNC block markers + content unchanged
- Confirm other body sections unchanged

## Risks

- **Low** — prose-only edit; no behavior change; functional routing preserved by global instruction.
- **Reversibility** — if the cross-reference turns out to be useful, can be re-added with accurate wording in a future change.
